facts.claim: Ho, Jain and Abbeel’s 2020 paper (DDPM) made high-quality pictures with a diffusion model. It set T = 1,000 steps for all its experiments, so making one picture runs the network 1,000 times.
Ho, Jain and Abbeel (2020) train the network to guess the noise that was added to a picture; their model for 32 × 32 photos (CIFAR-10) has 35.7 million weights, their larger models 114 million.
Song and colleagues (2021) describe a diffusion model as noise added gradually and then removed in reverse: “Creating noise from data is easy; creating data from noise is generative modeling.”

Classifier-free guidance (Ho and Salimans, 2022) trains one model with and without the label, dropping it at random, and mixes the two predictions as (1 + w) × labelled − w × unlabelled, trading sample diversity for quality.

The 2022 latent diffusion paper notes that the strongest models working on full-size pictures often took hundreds of days of graphics-chip time to train (150–1,000 days on V100 chips), and about 5 days on one A100 chip to make 50,000 pictures.

Latent diffusion (Rombach et al., 2022) runs the denoiser on a copy of the picture f times smaller each way, made and later restored by a network trained beforehand; the paper found f of 4 to 16 a good balance, with 4 and 8 best.

Flow matching (Lipman et al., 2023) trains a model to follow paths from noise to data; its optimal-transport paths are straight lines where diffusion’s curve, which the authors report makes training and drawing faster.
Consistency models (Song et al., 2023) turn noise into a picture in one step, can take a few steps for better quality, and can be trained by learning from an existing diffusion model.

Carlini and colleagues (2023) showed that diffusion models memorise individual training images and emit them when generating, extracting over a thousand training examples from state-of-the-art models.
Song, Meng and Ermon (2021) showed that the same trained model can draw in fewer steps (DDIM), making good pictures 10× to 50× faster in real time than DDPM, trading work for quality.
